spec_match.rationale: Teaches the exact alpha(from ... / calc(alpha * k)) grammar with a design-token use case, probes CSS.supports on that exact surface, and labels the rgb(from ...) and plain-rgb fallbacks honestly.

interactive.rationale: Changing the brand color re-derives all four token tiles plus the in-context scrim, focus ring, and disabled fill (CDP-driven brand change to #cc0011 re-tinted every surface, tiles included).

blurb_alignment.rationale: One brand token driving a family of translucent surfaces is exactly what the page now visibly does — including the headline tile row.

edge_cases.rationale: Three-tier fallback (alpha() -> rgb(from ...) -> plain rgba) is labelled at each tier, and the decl line prints both the derivation and the resolved computed value.

references.rationale: ChromeStatus 5070160203481088 (verified) and the css-color-5 relative-alpha anchor are linked.

conformance.rationale: The feature-level suite covers the exact alpha() grammar and fallback surfaces; suites are immutable and were not touched.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141.0.7390.37 via CDP: tile ::before computed backgrounds are the derived translucent colors at k 0.55/0.45/0.30/0.12, pixel samples prove tint-over-checkerboard (e.g. (222,110,116) after the fix vs flat (244,243,238) before), console clean except the environmental fonts.googleapis.com failure; the native alpha() branch is not exercisable in this browser (labelled fallback verified instead).

telemetry_health.rationale: The assert now samples the first tile fill's ::before — the surface visitors actually see — and still reports the fallback branch separately from a native pass.

design_system.rationale: All colors via CSS variables; the checkerboard uses --bg-stone/--bg-ivory; caption text pairs meet AA.

accessibility.rationale: Native color input with a visible label, tiles carry text captions (token name, k, purpose), the decl read-back is aria-live=polite, and the decorative scrim is aria-hidden.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 1280x1600 and 360x740 DPR3 touch via CDP emulation: tiles reflow via the auto-fill grid and there is no horizontal overflow on either class.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the native alpha() branch once it ships in a testable build
openQuestions.detail: This environment's Chromium 141 lacks alpha(), so the verified rendering path is the labelled rgb(from ...) fallback (visually identical for sRGB brands). When a Chrome build with alpha() enabled is available, confirm the native branch paints the tiles and that the 'tokens-alpha-derived' assert passes on the ::before sample.

guidanceConsulted.query: layering translucent color over checkerboard pattern with CSS background layers stacking context
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Control paint order with the element's own background layering instead of negative z-index pseudo-elements, which paint above their own element's background.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Moved the checkerboard onto .tile .fill's own background and painted the derived tint on an un-z-indexed ::before above it, fed via a --fill custom property; removed the misleading z-index:-1 + isolation pattern.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: Post-fix pixel samples show the tint compositing over the checkerboard at descending k values; pre-fix samples were flat checkerboard grey.

guidanceConsulted.query: aria-live region announcing updated results after select change
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce the outcome of a control change through one polite live region.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Kept the existing aria-live=polite decl read-back as the single announcement point for brand changes; no competing live regions added.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: decl text updates with the derived declaration plus the resolved computed color on brand input.

summary: Fixed in place with a minimal patch: the tiles' checkerboard ::before (z-index:-1 inside an isolated stacking context) painted above the fill's own background, so the four headline token tiles had never shown their tint in any browser. The checkerboard now lives on the element's own background with the derived tint on a pseudo-element above it, and the telemetry assert samples that visible tile layer instead of the always-working disabled button. Verified in headless Chromium 141 via CDP: computed ::before colors at k 0.55/0.45/0.30/0.12, pixel-proof of tint-over-checkerboard on desktop, live brand re-tint, clean console, no overflow on desktop or mobile. Native alpha() remains fallback-only in this environment, honestly labelled.
